body:
Records are currently stored in-memory only and lost when the session ends. This adds the ability to export records to Excel files, with each month's data saved to a separate file.

## Changes

### New utility: `utils/excelExport.ts`
- `groupByMonth(data)` - Groups records by month from "DD MM YYYY" date format
- `formatForExcel(data)` - Converts CaseData to Excel-friendly format with 14 columns
- `exportAllByMonth(data)` - Triggers staggered downloads of monthly Excel files
- `exportSingleMonth(data, monthKey)` - Exports a specific month's data

### App.tsx
- Added "Export to Excel" button (green) next to "Add Entry"
- Exports current `filteredData` grouped by month

### Dependencies
- Added `xlsx: ^0.18.5` (SheetJS)

## File naming convention
```
DC_Records_October_2025.xlsx
DC_Records_November_2025.xlsx
```

## Excel columns
Date, Reg No, Patient Name, Age, Case Type, Referrer, Investigations, Total Fee, Fee Paid, Fee Due, Discount, DC Amount, Canceled, Remark

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Overview
> Implement functionality to save records to separate Excel files, with each file containing records for a specific month.
> 
> ## Current Behavior
> Records are stored in-memory only and are lost when the browser session ends.
> 
> ## Desired Behavior
> Add the ability to export records to Excel files where:
> 1. Each month's records are saved to a **separate Excel file** (not sheets within one file)
> 2. File naming convention: `DC_Records_MonthName_Year.xlsx` (e.g., `DC_Records_October_2025.xlsx`, `DC_Records_November_2025.xlsx`)
> 3. Users can export all data at once, which downloads multiple files (one per month)
> 4. Users can also export just the current filtered/visible data
> 
> ## Technical Requirements
> 
> ### 1. Install the `xlsx` (SheetJS) library
> Add `"xlsx": "^0.18.5"` to package.json dependencies.
> 
> ### 2. Create Excel Export Utility (`utils/excelExport.ts`)
> Create a new utility file with these functions:
> 
> - `groupByMonth(data: CaseData[])` - Groups records by month based on the date field (format: "DD MM YYYY")
> - `getMonthName(month: number)` - Returns month name from month number
> - `formatForExcel(data: CaseData[])` - Converts CaseData to Excel-friendly format with proper column headers
> - `exportAllByMonth(data: CaseData[])` - Exports each month's data to a separate Excel file (triggers multiple downloads)
> - `exportSingleMonth(data: CaseData[], monthKey: string)` - Exports a specific month's data to one Excel file
> 
> ### 3. Excel File Format
> Each Excel file should have these columns:
> - Date
> - Reg No
> - Patient Name
> - Age
> - Case Type
> - Referrer
> - Investigations
> - Total Fee
> - Fee Paid
> - Fee Due
> - Discount
> - DC Amount
> - Canceled (Yes/No)
> - Remark
> 
> Set appropriate column widths for readability.
> 
> ### 4. Update App.tsx
> - Import the export functions and Download icon from lucide-react
> - Add an "Export to Excel" button in the header section (next to "Add Entry" button)
> - Style the button with green background (`bg-green-600`) to differentiate from Add Entry
> - When clicked, export the current `filteredData` grouped by month to separate files
> 
> ### 5. Date Handling
> The record date format is "DD MM YYYY" (e.g., "01 10 2025" for October 1, 2025):
> - parts[0] = Day
> - parts[1] = Month  
> - parts[2] = Year
> 
> Group by `parts[1]` (month) and `parts[2]` (year) to create monthly files.
> 
> ## Example Output
> If records exist for October 2025 and November 2025, clicking "Export to Excel" should download:
> - `DC_Records_October_2025.xlsx` (containing all October records)
> - `DC_Records_November_2025.xlsx` (containing all November records)


</details>

author: parq254
body:
**Understanding of Backend Development:** I implemented this using the CQRS pattern. This separates the action of modifying data from reading it. I created a specific `AddNoteToBudgetCommand` to carry the data, and a `AddNoteToBudgetHandler` to perform the logic. This keeps the code clean and follows the Single Responsibility Principle.

### Design Choices:

- **Validation:** I added a check in the handler to ensure empty notes are not saved, preserving data integrity.

- **Dependencies:** I used the `getRepository` from the toolkit to access the database, ensuring I didn't hardcode database logic directly into the handler.

**Deployment & Serverless:** In this architecture, this Handler would likely be deployed as a Google Cloud Function.

- **Scaling:** Serverless is ideal for this because it auto-scales. If nobody adds notes, the function sleep. If 10,000 users add notes at once, the cloud provider automatically spins up 10,000 instances of this handler to process them in parallel, then shuts them down.

author: thomask33
body:
## Summary

Reintroduces the ORPC refactoring originally merged in #763 and reverted in #777.

This replaces the custom IPC layer with [oRPC](https://orpc.unnoq.com/) for type-safe RPC between browser/renderer and backend processes.

## Why it was reverted (#777)

The original migration caused regressions:
- Streaming content delay from ORPC schema validation
- Field stripping issues in sendMessage output  
- Auto-compaction trigger deletion

## What's different this time

- Rebased onto latest main which includes fixes developed post-revert
- Conflict resolution preserves upstream features added after revert:
  - Workspace name collision retry with hash suffix (#779)
  - Mux Gateway coupon code handling with default models
  - AWS Bedrock credential nested structure

## Key Changes

### Architecture
- **New ORPC router** (`src/node/orpc/router.ts`) - Central router with Zod schemas
- **Schema definitions** (`src/common/orpc/schemas.ts`) - Shared validation
- **ServiceContainer** (`src/node/services/serviceContainer.ts`) - DI container
- **React integration** (`src/browser/orpc/react.tsx`) - `ORPCProvider` and `useORPC()`

### Transport
- **Desktop (Electron)**: MessagePort-based RPC via `@orpc/server/message-port`
- **Server mode**: HTTP + WebSocket via `@orpc/server/node` and `@orpc/server/ws`
- Auth middleware with timing-safe token comparison

### Removed
- `src/browser/api.ts` (old HTTP/WS client)
- `src/node/services/ipcMain.ts` (old IPC handler registration)
- Old IPC method definitions in preload.ts

## Test plan

- [x] Run `make typecheck` - passes locally
- [x] Run `make test` - verify existing tests pass
- [x] Manual testing of desktop app (Electron)
- [x] Manual testing of server mode (browser)
- [x] Verify streaming chat works without delays
- [x] Verify auto-compaction triggers correctly

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive order management feature to the commerce gateway. It adds the ability for users to create orders from their cart, view their orders, and for admins to manage and update orders. The implementation includes new controller endpoints, service logic, data transfer objects (DTOs), mappers, and repository methods to support these operations.

**Order Management Feature Implementation:**

*Major API and Service Layer Additions:*
- Introduced `OrderController` with endpoints for creating orders, retrieving user and all orders, updating order status, canceling orders, and fetching order details. This controller uses OpenAPI annotations for documentation.
- Implemented `OrderService` and its corresponding `OrderServiceImpl` with business logic to handle order creation, retrieval, status updates, cancellation, and detailed order fetching. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b2a40f43d3c49c821d8d9590c6c75aaf240d4725416a032485ebe44f6c8160ccR3-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a3ed55dd23dc2f6cd21dea8f6c0bde445799895794857f776291db9fe5f60e62R3-R108)

*Data Transfer Objects and Mappers:*
- Added DTOs for order requests (`OrderRequest`), order responses (`OrderResponse`), detailed order responses (`OrderDetailResponse`), and order item responses (`OrderItemResponse`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2d30b658fd5f907e8bf5a092a14634bbda011eaf332a2b15e5a110eb030874b2R1-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-096a6b95edd780377b0356549c32039700661abfab450ae3624d4ae6d4de7ab3R1-R22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b370a16214f2e7ce0581bb925afaa7f36e503427c5f4c767a7080d02e2fd9746R1-R24) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2e72817c5d8cc6dd23e3186fcc2ad7a1b3a7dc5b825c586512c8e4329b969f74R1-R14)
- Created `OrderMapper` to convert between entity models and DTOs, including logic for calculating order item totals and assembling detailed order responses.

*Repository Enhancements:*
- Extended repositories to support new queries:
    - [`OrderRepository`](diffhunk://#diff-dc80c2b3af25019efbbd9616015a9c476f6b7775eaa54e2a9be379146e37ed6aR4-R15): Added method to find orders by user.
    - [`OrderItemRepository`](diffhunk://#diff-d5b282a83160a2cf2bb9e91a908479558cc755ad3732833a4eec0ee86ef57a73R3-R15): Added method to find order items by order.
    - [`CartItemRepository`](diffhunk://#diff-ab0ca971c68d0f3ade014c016569ff7dba6a25d3886bd0732032e8c920d5a2a5R3-R23): Added methods to delete cart items by cart ID and to find items by cart.
    - [`CartRepository`](diffhunk://#diff-bd0c32443999027f056ad8570374b267a077d4d2e845ce6b1bcf6c3584de0870L14): Cleaned up and ensured method for finding cart by user.

*Cart Service Improvements:*
- Updated `CartServiceImpl` to properly implement `getMyCart` and `clearCart`, ensuring cart retrieval and clearing are handled for the current user and integrate with the new order flow.

author: mdpearce
body:
## Summary
This PR adds Gradle Play Publisher plugin configuration to automate publishing to the Google Play Store.

## Changes
- ✅ Added Gradle Play Publisher plugin (v3.10.1)
- ✅ Configured default publishing to internal track with draft status (for testing)
- ✅ Added comprehensive documentation in `docs/play_store_publishing.md`
- ✅ Updated `.gitignore` to protect service account credentials
- ✅ Incremented versionCode to 12

## Configuration
- **Default Track**: Internal testing
- **Release Status**: Draft (won't auto-publish until changed to 'completed')
- **Credentials**: Expects `app/play-store-credentials.json` (protected by .gitignore)

## Next Steps
To use this:
1. Create a service account in Google Play Console
2. Download the JSON credentials
3. Place as `app/play-store-credentials.json`
4. Run `./gradlew publishReleaseBundle` to publish

See `docs/play_store_publishing.md` for detailed setup instructions.

## Testing
- ✅ Build file compiles successfully
- ✅ Plugin resolves correctly
- ✅ No secrets committed (verified .gitignore)

author: tsuchiya2
body:
## Summary

- Add GitHub Actions workflow that automatically creates releases when code is merged to main
- Automatically increments patch version (e.g., v1.0.17 → v1.0.18)
- Generates release notes with merged PR information

Closes #199

## Changes

- Add `.github/workflows/release.yml`

## How it works

1. Triggered on push to `main` branch
2. Gets latest tag (defaults to v0.0.0 if none)
3. Increments patch version
4. Creates GitHub Release with:
   - PR title and number in release notes
   - Changelog link comparing versions

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge this PR to main
- [ ] Verify new release v1.0.18 is created automatically
- [ ] Verify release notes contain PR information

author: ambient-labs
body:
## Summary

Removes the lint-staged dependency and replaces it with a simple shell script that runs ESLint and Prettier directly on staged files.

## Changes

- Add `scripts/pre-commit.sh` that:
  - Gets staged files via `git diff --cached`
  - Runs ESLint `--fix` on `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx` files
  - Runs Prettier `--write` on all staged files
  - Re-stages fixed files automatically
  - Supports `SKIP_PRE_COMMIT=1` to bypass checks
- Update `simple-git-hooks` to use the new script
- Remove `lint-staged` from devDependencies

## Benefits

- One less dependency
- More explicit control over what runs
- Easier to understand and debug
- Consistent with other pre-commit hook patterns

## Test plan

- [x] Shell script syntax validated with `bash -n`
- [ ] Manual testing with staged files

Fixes #79

author: ambient-labs
body:
## Summary

Makes local pre-commit checks identical to CI by running all tests and security scans before commit.

## Changes

Replaces `lint-staged` with a comprehensive pre-commit script that runs the same checks as CI:

### Sequential (must complete first)
- ESLint and Prettier on staged code files (re-stages fixed files)

### Parallel (path-filtered, run concurrently)
- Unit tests (frontend and DSP, if respective source files changed)
- Integration tests (if DSP or tests/ changed)
- Semgrep security scan (if code files changed, requires Docker)
- Native build (if native/ files changed)

## Performance

| Check | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| ESLint + Prettier | ~5s | Sequential |
| Unit tests | ~5-10s | Parallel |
| Integration tests | ~10-20s | Parallel |
| Semgrep | ~10-30s | Parallel, Docker overhead |
| Native build | ~60-120s | Only on native changes |

**Total: ~35s for most commits** (dominated by slowest parallel check)

## Skip Option

For emergencies:
```bash
SKIP_PRE_COMMIT=1 git commit -m "message"
```

## Test plan

- [x] Shell script syntax validated with `bash -n`
- [ ] Manual testing with different file combinations

Fixes #80

body:
# Add configurable predicate ordering in serialisation

Closes #1 

## Changes

- **New `core/predicate_order.py`**: `PredicateOrderSpec`, `PredicateOrderConfig`, subject classification, and ordering logic
- **Updated `core/serialiser.py`**: `serialise_turtle()` accepts optional `predicate_order` parameter
- **Updated `core/profile.py`**: Loads `predicate_order` from YAML, adds `get_predicate_order()` method
- **Updated `cli.py`**: Passes predicate ordering through to serialiser

## Usage

```yaml
predicate_order:
  classes:
    first: [rdfs:label, rdfs:comment]
    last: [rdfs:subClassOf]
  properties:
    first: [rdfs:label, rdfs:comment, rdfs:domain, rdfs:range]
    last: [rdfs:subPropertyOf]
```

Can be set at config level (applies to all profiles) or per-profile (overrides config).

## Testing

- 20 new unit tests in `tests/test_predicate_order.py`
- Backward compatible: no `predicate_order` config = existing alphabetical behaviour

author: beltvigea
body:
CRITICAL FIX: This resolves the root cause of event reporting not working.

Problem:
- BambuStatusSubscriber was initialized before config_manager
- Config file never had backend_url saved
- EventReporter couldn't initialize without backend_url
- Result: No events were ever reported to backend

Changes:
1. Move config_manager initialization BEFORE statusSubscriber creation
2. Automatically save backend URL to config file on first run
3. Ensures EventReporter has all required credentials (backend_url, api_key, recipient_id)

Before this fix, logs showed:
  ⚠️  EventReporter NOT initialized (missing credentials)
     base_url: ❌
     api_key: ✅
     recipient_id: ✅

After this fix, EventReporter will initialize successfully with all credentials.

This was discovered through the verbose debug logging added in the previous commit. The heartbeat was working because it used a hardcoded URL, but event reporting required the URL to be in the config file for BambuStatusSubscriber to access it.

author: jaimeveleiro
body:
## Fix: Date Format (Apple Compatibility)

### Summary

Changed the date format from `'**YYYY, Month**'` (e.g., `'2025, March'`) to the standard `'**YYYY-MM-DD**'` (e.g., `'2025-03-01'`).

### Rationale

The previous format caused parsing errors and **incorrect display on iOS/Apple devices (Safari)**. This change ensures proper date interpretation across all platforms, resolving the Apple-specific rendering issue.

author: schnetziomi5
body:
The missing globals/empty environment bug was caused by `VPUI_core` or `CPK` being included in the `LoadScreen` context. This context gets discarded at some point ingame, at latest when the leader screen is opened for the first time. However the functions saved by `VPUI` or `CPK` to `MapModData` still point to that (probably not just empty but invalid) environment as their global table, causing the bug.

By setting `MapModData` to nil in the `LoadScreen` context, `VPUI` and `CPK` (and any other similar files) are prevented from saving anything there at this point. Instead they seem to be next loaded from the `Civilopedia` context, which is a proper ingame context...

This change implements the standard Quake 2 connection handshake protocol in the dedicated server.
It adds `clientConnect` and `clientDisconnect` to the Game API to manage client admission and cleanup.
The `DedicatedServer` now correctly parses `connect` commands, validates them via the game API, sends `svc_serverdata`, and waits for the `begin` command before spawning the client entity.
This replaces the previous placeholder logic where clients were spawned immediately upon sending a move command.

author: copilot
body:
Full-stack web application for recognizing handwritten Urdu characters (36 alphabets + 10 digits) using a CNN model. Users can upload images or draw characters on canvas for prediction.

## Backend (FastAPI)

- **API endpoints**: `/api/v1/predict`, `/api/v1/predict/canvas`, `/api/v1/classes`, `/health`
- **CNN architecture**: 4 conv blocks (32→64→128→256 filters) + 2 dense layers (512→256) with BatchNorm, Dropout
- **Services**: Singleton model service, image preprocessing (grayscale, 64x64 resize, normalize)
- **ML pipeline**: Training, evaluation, preprocessing, augmentation scripts in `ml/`
- **Infrastructure**: Custom logger with rotating file handler, Pydantic settings, custom exceptions

## Frontend (React/TypeScript/Vite)

- **Components**: `ImageUploader` (react-dropzone), `DrawingCanvas` (HTML5 canvas), `PredictionResult` (confidence bars)
- **Pages**: Home (prediction UI), About, How It Works
- **Hooks**: `usePrediction` for prediction state management
- **Styling**: TailwindCSS with RTL support for Urdu text

## DevOps

- Docker Compose with separate containers for frontend/backend
- Nginx config for SPA routing and API proxy

## Usage

```bash
# Backend
cd backend && uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# Frontend  
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev
```

API example:
```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/predict" -F "file=@character.png"
# {"prediction": "ا", "confidence": 0.95, "top_5": [...], "processing_time_ms": 45.2}
```

body:
**Improvements**
_1. Google Login – Required Fields Validation_
Updated the Google Sign-In flow so users must have all required profile fields completed. If any mandatory field is missing, the user will not be able to complete a purchase or view their orders. This ensures consistent user data and prevents incomplete profiles from accessing critical features.

_2. Order Amount Precision (2 Decimals)_
Product prices are now always stored and displayed with exactly two decimal places, both when creating and updating products. All related orders will also display totals rounded to two decimals for consistent pricing across the system.

_3. Dashboard – New KPI Added_
A new KPI was added to the Dashboard to show the total sales amount within the selected date range, eliminating the need to manually add values for each day.

**How to Test It**
_1. Google Login Required Fields_

Log in using Google with a user missing one or more required fields.

Try completing a purchase or viewing orders — both actions should be blocked.

Fill in all required fields.

Retry the actions and they should now work correctly.

_2. Order Amount Precision_

Create a product with more than two decimals in the price (e.g., 12.9876). It should store/display as 12.99.

Update a product using more than two decimals. It should still store 2 decimals.

Create an order with those products and verify the total also displays two decimals.

_3. Dashboard KPI_

Open the Dashboard and select any date range.

Confirm the new KPI appears showing the total amount for that range.

Compare it with manually added daily totals to verify correctness.

author: gdy23319
body:
Related to yzfzzz/SGBM-Python#27

### PR内容介绍
在/SGBM(Python）下，增加了一个实时性更强的sgbm-video-realtime.py作为示例程序。

它通过一个独立线程，每0.01s进行一次抓帧，保存最新帧。在对实时性要求高的场景下，实测发现这种方式可以降低延迟。

（当然，如果程序帧率超高（得大于摄像头帧率30FPS），可能不需要独立线程抓帧，按原逻辑也能做到实时性很好。但是如果在jetson nano上，帧率较低，这样写是需要的，否则延迟无法忍受）

为了演示，sgbm-video-realtime.py像原示例程序sgbm-video.py一样从示例视频car.avi读帧，尽管这会导致视频很快播放完。

可以连接摄像头进行实验(需要把camreader那里的src改成摄像头名称（一般是0或者1）），实测大大降低了延迟。
### 和sgbm-video.py的区别
sgbm-video-readtime.py和sgbm-video.py主要的区别是：
1.添加了摄像头线程类
```
# --------------------------摄像头线程类---------------------------------------------------------
#   ~100FPS刷新，始终保留最新帧
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CameraReader:
    def __init__(self, src='SGBM(Python)\car.avi'):
        self.cap = cv2.VideoCapture(src)
        self.cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH, 1280)
        self.cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT, 480)
        if not self.cap.isOpened():
            raise ValueError(f"cannot access camera: {src}")

        self.latest_frame = None
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.running = True

        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._update, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    def _update(self):
        while self.running:
            ret, frame = self.cap.read()
            if ret:
                with self.lock:
                    self.latest_frame = frame
            else:
                time.sleep(0.01)

    def get_latest_frame(self):
        with self.lock:
            return None if self.latest_frame is None else self.latest_frame.copy()

    def release(self):
        self.running = False
        self.thread.join(timeout=1.0)
        self.cap.release()
```
2.主要逻辑变成调用这个线程类
`cam = CameraReader('SGBM(Python)\car.avi')`

`frame = cam.get_latest_frame()`

### 环境配置
添加了requirement.txt。
```
numpy==1.23.0
opencv-python==4.5.1.48
```
注：并未改变摄像头参数（还是对应示例视频car.avi的参数），应该可以直接运行查看效果

body:
Long filenames (hashes) overflow in ResultOverlay dialog. Users report 100% predictions look unprofessional.

## Changes

### GUI: Filename truncation in `ResultOverlay.setup_ui()`
- Truncate filenames >30 chars to `first_15...last_10` format
- Preserves file extension visibility

```python
if len(filename) > 30:
    display_name = filename[:15] + "..." + filename[-10:]
```

### Prediction Engine: Realistic probability mapping in `predict_file()`
- Map probabilities >95% → uniform(0.96, 0.995)
- Maintain existing 1.5% floor for safe files
- Clamp final output at 99.9%

```python
if malware_probability > 0.95:
    malware_probability = np.random.uniform(0.96, 0.995)
malware_probability = max(malware_probability, PROBABILITY_FLOOR)
malware_probability = min(malware_probability, 0.999)
```

### Tests
- `test_filename_truncation.py` — boundary cases, extension preservation
- `test_realistic_probability_mapping.py` — range validation, floor/clamp behavior

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> I am finalizing the Malware Detection System. I need to fix 2 specific issues based on user feedback:
> 
> GUI Layout Bug: In the ResultOverlay dialog, long filenames (like hashes) are overflowing or being cut off, making the UI look broken.
> 
> Probability Range: Users find "100%" predictions unprofessional. They want high-confidence malware predictions to fall realistically within the 96.0% to 99.5% range.
> 
> Request: Refactor the code to fix both issues.
> 
> Task 1: Refactor src/modern_gui.py (Fix Text Overflow)
> 
> Target: ResultOverlay class, setup_ui method.
> 
> Logic: Before creating conclusion_label, apply truncation to the filename if it is too long.
> 
> Condition: If len(filename) > 30.
> 
> Action: Create a display_name keeping the first 15 chars and last 10 chars (e.g., very_long_file_na...extension.exe).
> 
> Usage: Use this display_name for the conclusion_label text to ensure it fits the dialog.
> 
> Task 2: Refactor src/prediction_engine.py (Realistic Probability)
> 
> Target: predict_file method.
> 
> Logic: Update the probability calculation logic for both individual models and the final score:
> 
> Get raw probability.
> 
> Apply "Realistic High-Confidence Mapping":
> 
> If prob > 0.95 (Very confident): Map it to a random value between 0.96 and 0.995 (e.g., 96.4%, 98.7%, 99.2%).
> 
> Code: if prob > 0.95: prob = np.random.uniform(0.96, 0.995)
> 
> Apply "Safe Floor": Ensure low scores don't hit absolute 0.
> 
> Code: prob = max(0.015, prob) (Minimum 1.5%).
> 
> Final Clamp: Ensure prob is strictly < 1.0.

After that, all future releases will create a new image without the need for more manual intervention

Fixes: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/169113

Correctly propagate verification failure when `NVVM::RequiresSMInterface` check fails during `gpu.module` verification.
Previously, the walk was interrupted but the function returned `success()`, causing a mismatch between the emitted diagnostic and the return status. This led to assertion failures in Python bindings which expect `failure()` when diagnostics are emitted.

body:
###Backend development process & design choices

Created the budget-notes domain manually under libs/model/budgetting/budget-notes/src/lib/domain to encapsulate the AddNote functionality. I implemented the AddNoteToBudgetCommand to carry the necessary data for adding a note, and the AddNoteToBudgetHandler to perform basic validation and invoke the repository method to persist the note. Dependencies such as the repository are accessed via the handler’s toolkit, which follows the repository pattern established in the repo. Some parts of the handler’s integration with the repository were scaffolded, but I focused mainly on the structural setup and core logic due to time constraints.

###Deployment of the handler

Following the repo’s architecture, this handler would be deployed as a Firebase Function. Using the existing Nx/Firebase tooling, the function can be included in the build and deployed along with other backend functions. Any changes to the handler would be automatically reflected after redeploying the function using firebase deploy.

###Serverless deployment & scaling

Serverless deployment allows this handler to scale automatically based on demand. Each invocation is stateless and independent, meaning multiple requests can be processed concurrently without requiring manual server provisioning. This ensures the function can handle spikes in usage efficiently and cost-effectively, only consuming resources when actually invoked.

body:
# Add ingest sub-module for book ingestion pipeline

## Summary

This PR adds a complete book ingestion system as a sub-module for the librarian project. The system processes DRM-free EPUBs and PDFs, extracts metadata using an LLM committee of 7 specialized agents, and stores everything in a Qdrant vector database for RAG-based retrieval.

Key components:
- **Extractors**: EPUB/PDF parsing using pymupdf and ebooklib
- **LLM Committee**: 7 agents (bibliography, genre/tags, overview, chapter summaries, key quotes, themes, technical concepts)
- **VLM Integration**: Qwen2.5-VL-72B for OCR and image summarization
- **Semantic Chunking**: 500-2000 tokens with 20% overlap using LangChain
- **Vector Storage**: Qdrant with BGE-base-en-v1.5 embeddings
- **CLI**: Commands for ingestion, search, listing, and deletion
- **Batch Processing**: Script with progress tracking and resume support

Designed for GB10 hardware (128GB unified memory) with concurrent VLM (~40GB) and LLM (~40GB) loading.

## Updates since last revision

- Fixed `LogContext` usage in `pipeline.py` - now correctly passes `logger` and `operation` as required positional arguments
- Updated README.md to reflect correct 128GB unified memory spec (was incorrectly showing 64GB)
- Added pseudocode documentation for Phase 2 components in `docs/`:
  - `pseudocode_website.md`: FastAPI backend + React frontend for browsing, search, per-book chat, and checkout
  - `pseudocode_slack_bot.md`: Bolt Python bot with threaded conversations, RAG-based Q&A, and checkout system

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [x] ~~**BUG: LogContext usage mismatch**~~ - Fixed in latest commit

- [x] ~~**README/requirements inconsistency**~~ - Fixed in latest commit

- [ ] **No unit tests included** - All code is untested. Recommend testing on actual GB10 hardware with real books before merging.

- [ ] **LLM prompts need validation** - The agent system prompts are complex and may need tuning based on actual model outputs. Test with sample books to verify quality.

- [ ] **Verify Qdrant schema** - The payload indexes and search filters should be tested against a real Qdrant instance.

**Recommended Test Plan:**
1. Set up vLLM with a quantized model and Qdrant locally (or request SSH access to GB10)
2. Run `librarian-ingest ingest /path/to/sample.epub --verbose --debug`
3. Verify chunks are stored correctly with `librarian-ingest list-books` and `librarian-ingest search "test query"`
4. Test batch processing with a small directory of books

### Notes

- This is Phase 1 of the librarian project (ingestion only). Phase 2 (Slack bot + web UI) will be built separately.
- The pseudocode docs are planning materials for Phase 2, not functional code.
- Testing will be difficult without the target hardware. Jack mentioned he can provide SSH access to an ASUS Ascent GX10 when ready.
- The code passes `ruff check` lint validation.

author: alaviss
body:
## Summary
Fix stack corruption due to oversized  `copyMem`  when casting from/to
imported types.

## Details
Type sizes encoded in AST and MIR both use special negative values to
denote either an error or unknown size. This detail is then picked up by
CGIR and rendered verbatim into C code, causing  `nimCopyMem`  to be
called with an excessively large value, corrupting the stack.

This change renders the required computation directly into CGIR when the
size could not be computed by the compiler for casts, solving the
problem.

Fixes https://github.com/nim-works/nimskull/issues/1661

body:
**Improvements**
_1. Google Login – Required Fields Validation_
Updated the Google Sign-In flow so users must have all required profile fields completed. If any mandatory field is missing, the user will not be able to complete a purchase or view their orders. This ensures consistent user data and prevents incomplete profiles from accessing critical features.

_2. Order Amount Precision (2 Decimals)_
Product prices are now always stored and displayed with exactly two decimal places, both when creating and updating products. All related orders will also display totals rounded to two decimals for consistent pricing across the system.

_3. Dashboard – New KPI Added_
A new KPI was added to the Dashboard to show the total sales amount within the selected date range, eliminating the need to manually add values for each day.

**How to Test It**
_1. Google Login Required Fields_

Log in using Google with a user missing one or more required fields.

Try completing a purchase or viewing orders — both actions should be blocked.

Fill in all required fields.

Retry the actions and they should now work correctly.

_2. Order Amount Precision_

Create a product with more than two decimals in the price (e.g., 12.9876). It should store/display as 12.99.

Update a product using more than two decimals. It should still store 2 decimals.

Create an order with those products and verify the total also displays two decimals.

_3. Dashboard KPI_

Open the Dashboard and select any date range.

Confirm the new KPI appears showing the total amount for that range.

Compare it with manually added daily totals to verify correctness.

This PR enhances the WordPress plugin parser to detect when an API endpoint handler verifies a custom nonce. If a verification call is found (via `check_ajax_referer`, `check_admin_referer`, or `wp_verify_nonce`), the parser now identifies the corresponding code that generates this nonce (via `wp_create_nonce`) and includes it in the output reports (TXT and JSON).

- `parser.php`: Added `NonceCreationIndexer` and `NonceVerificationFinder` visitors.
- `parser.php`: Updated main execution loop to perform a pre-pass for nonce indexing and a post-pass for verification matching.
- `parser.php`: Updated `Endpoint` class to store and display nonce generation code.

author: stunningpixels
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) editor powered by Lexical, replacing the previous plain text inputs for task creation, follow-ups, and inline editing throughout the app. It also implements a new "scratch" storage system for auto-saving draft content and adds support for queuing follow-up messages.

### Key Changes

**New WYSIWYG Editor (`frontend/src/components/ui/wysiwyg.tsx`)**
- Rich text editing with Lexical: bold, italic, strikethrough, blockquotes, lists, headings
- Inline and multi-line code blocks with syntax highlighting via `@lexical/code`
- Horizontal scrolling for code blocks that exceed container width
- File/tag picker triggered by `@` mentions (similar to previous FileSearchTextArea)
- Image support with thumbnails, preview dialogs, and markdown import/export
- Keyboard shortcuts: CMD+Enter for submit, Shift+CMD+Enter for secondary action
- Optional toolbar for formatting controls
- Read-only mode with copy button for displaying rendered content

**Scratch Storage System (replaces Drafts)**
- New `scratch` table and API for persisting editor content in real-time
- WebSocket-based streaming for live updates (`/api/scratch/:type/:id/stream`)
- Stores content as markdown for better serialization
- Used for task follow-up drafts, task creation dialogs, and inline retry editors
- Graceful error handling for malformed scratch data
- Fixed timing issue where scratch wasn't reset if execution startup was slow

**Queued Follow-Up Messages**
- In-memory queue service for scheduling follow-up messages
- Queue a message while an agent is working; it auto-sends when the current task completes
- Cancel queued messages before they execute
- Queue is cleared if task fails or is stopped (prevents unintended executions)

**Image Handling Improvements**
- Images uploaded to follow-ups are immediately copied to the task worktree's `.vibe-images/` folder
- Relative paths (`.vibe-images/...`) stored in markdown instead of absolute paths
- New endpoints: image metadata (`/api/task-attempts/:id/images/:path/info`) and proxy (`/api/task-attempts/:id/images/:path`)
- Image preview dialog on click with full-size view

**UI/UX Improvements**
- Restored retry task functionality that was previously removed
- Refactored variant selection with cleaner `useDefaultVariant` hook
- Improved styling for task dialog, approval messages, and follow-up box
- Consistent font styling across editor components

**Cleanup & Refactoring**
- Removed old `FileSearchTextArea` component and related code
- Removed old `MarkdownRenderer` in favor of WYSIWYG read-only mode
- Deleted legacy `drafts` system (table, service, routes)
- Consolidated markdown rendering into single component
- Moved follow-up related hooks to dedicated directory

### Files Changed

- **100 files** changed with **+4,531 / -4,755** lines
- **64 commits** spanning backend (Rust crates) and frontend (React/TypeScript)

### Database Migrations

- `20251120000001_refactor_to_scratch.sql` - Creates new scratch table
- `20251129155145_drop_drafts_table.sql` - Removes deprecated drafts table

## Test Plan

- [ ] Create a new task using the task form dialog - verify rich text formatting works
- [ ] Send follow-up messages with formatted text, code blocks, and images
- [ ] Verify code blocks scroll horizontally when content is wide
- [ ] Verify scratch auto-saves content and persists across page navigation
- [ ] Test queuing a follow-up message while agent is running, verify it sends after completion
- [ ] Cancel a queued message and verify it doesn't execute
- [ ] Stop a running task and verify queued messages are cleared
- [ ] Upload images in follow-ups, verify they appear with thumbnails and can be previewed
- [ ] Test inline retry editor with the new WYSIWYG - verify retry functionality works
- [ ] Verify keyboard shortcuts (CMD+Enter to send, Shift+CMD+Enter for secondary action)
- [ ] Test @-mention file picker in the editor

## Summary

This PR adds the ability to edit and remove messages sent to individual users in the admin interface, similar to the existing functionality for announcements.

Previously, admins could only send messages to users but had no way to edit or delete them after sending. This change adds:

- `EditMessageHandler` - handles POST requests to edit a message's subject and text
- `DeleteMessageHandler` - handles DELETE requests to remove a message
- Updated `participation.html` template with "Edit" and "Remove" links for each message

The implementation follows the same patterns used for announcements in `contestannouncement.py` and `announcements.html`.

## Updates since last revision

Addressed reviewer comments:
- Fixed delete redirect path to use URL builder (`self.url(...)`) instead of hardcoded relative path `../../../../edit`
- Added whitespace validation for subject input - now strips whitespace and rejects whitespace-only subjects

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify the JavaScript `utils.announcement_edit_toggle()` function works correctly for messages** - The template reuses this function from announcements; test that clicking "Edit" properly shows the edit form and populates it with the existing message content
- [ ] **Test the delete functionality end-to-end** - Click "Remove" on a message and verify it's deleted and the page redirects correctly back to the participation edit page
- [ ] **Test whitespace-only subject validation** - Try editing a message with a subject containing only spaces; verify it shows an error notification
- [ ] **Verify authorization** - Confirm that only admins with `PERMISSION_MESSAGING` can edit/delete messages

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Log into the admin interface
2. Navigate to a contest → Users → select a user → edit participation
3. Send a new message to the user
4. Click "Edit" on the message, modify subject/text, submit - verify changes are saved
5. Try editing with whitespace-only subject - verify error notification appears

author: lochipi
body:
# Refactor: Budget viewer with Angular 16 Signals

**Summary:**  
I went through the codebase, and noticed that we can't use Siganals in Angular 15(as per our project's version), so I upgraded to **Angular 16**  firstand refactored state management to use **Signals**. Replaced old RxJS patterns, manual subscriptions, and constructor DI with modern reactive primitives and `inject()`. Components now have fine-grained reactivity, automatic cleanup, and simpler templates.

**Changes:**  
- Project was on Angular 15.0.4, which doesn't have Signals so I upgraded project to **Angular 16**.  
- Upgraded to Angular 16 to get access to `signal()`, `computed()`, `effect()`, `toSignal()`, and `input()`

- Replaced constructor DI with `inject()`
- Converted RxJS observables to signals using `toSignal()`
- Created `computed()` signal for derived state (combining overview + budgets)
- Added `effect()` for logging side effects
- Created `signal()` for UI state (showFilter toggle)

- Replaced `@Input()` with signal-based `input.required<>()`
- Used `effect()` to react to input changes
- Removed manual subscription management (no more SubSink needed)

- Changed from `*ngIf` to `@if` control flow syntax
- Removed async pipe usage (signals don't need it)
- Updated property bindings to call signals: `allBudgets()` instead of `allBudgets$ | async`

**What's better about React Hooks:**
- Simpler - just functions, no framework magic
- Huge ecosystem of custom hooks
- Easier to compose (hooks in hooks)

**What's better about Angular Signals:**
- **Automatic dependency tracking** - No manual dependency arrays to mess up
- **No stale closures** - Classic React bug that doesn't exist with Signals
- **Fine-grained updates** - Only affected parts re-render (React re-renders whole component)
- **Easier debugging** - Signal always shows current value

To summarize this all, almost all modern frameworks are moving toward fine-grained reactivity (Vue 3, Svelte, Solid.js, now Angular). It's faster and uses less memory than zone.js or virtual DOM diffing.

## my design choices

**toSignal() for Observable → Signal conversion:**
The stores return RxJS observables (for HTTP/Firestore streams). Used `toSignal()` to convert them into signals so we get automatic subscriptions and cleanup.

**computed() for derived state:**
Instead of `combineLatest().pipe(map())`, used `computed()` to combine overview and budgets. Cleaner syntax, auto-updates when dependencies change.

**effect() for side effects:**
Logging shouldn't be in the computed logic (keeps it pure). Used `effect()` to run logger when budgets change.

**input.required() for child component:**
Child component receives data via signal inputs instead of `@Input()`. More type-safe and reactive.


**Benefits:**  
- No manual subscription management → zero memory leaks  
- Clear, declarative state flow  
- Fine-grained reactivity → only affected parts re-render  
- Future-proof architecture for Angular 16+  

**Files modified:**  
I've touched a few components files including ts, and html files where we've consumed it.


### Some of the resources I used:
- https://angular.dev/update-guide?v=15.0-16.0&l=3
- and some research on StackOverflow and online search, and a little help of AI to explain ambiguous functions

author: ericfitz
body:
## Summary
Fixes `IllegalArgumentException: count is negative: -1` that occurs when CATS generates HTML reports for API responses containing malformed JSON with extra closing brackets.

## Root Cause
The `SimpleJsonFormatter.formatJsonString()` method was calling `String.repeat(indentLevel - 1)` on line 57 without checking if `indentLevel` was 0, resulting in a negative repeat count.

This occurred when:
- API responses contained malformed JSON (e.g., `{"key":"value"}}`)
- The formatter encountered more closing brackets than opening brackets
- The `indentLevel` counter reached 0 before all closing brackets were processed

## Changes
- **Fix:** Added `Math.max(0, indentLevel - 1)` guard in [SimpleJsonFormatter.java:57](https://github.com/Endava/cats/blob/master/src/main/java/com/endava/cats/util/SimpleJsonFormatter.java#L57)
- **Tests:** Added 3 test cases for malformed JSON edge cases:
  - `shouldHandleMalformedJsonWithExtraClosingBrackets()` - tests `{...}}`
  - `shouldHandleMalformedJsonWithExtraClosingSquareBrackets()` - tests `[...]]`
  - `shouldHandleNestedStructures()` - ensures normal nested JSON still works

## Test Results
```
[INFO] Tests run: 8, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
```

All tests pass, including the 3 new edge case tests.

## Impact
- **Before:** CATS would crash with `MustacheException` when generating HTML reports for malformed JSON responses
- **After:** CATS gracefully handles malformed JSON and continues generating reports

## Files Changed
- `src/main/java/com/endava/cats/util/SimpleJsonFormatter.java` - 1 line changed
- `src/test/java/com/endava/cats/util/SimpleJsonFormatterTest.java` - 23 lines added

author: nicktomlin
body:
Lots of macros and implementation-y stuff here.


Interesting tidbits:

Precedence. I'm still wrapping my head around the pratt parser + stack thing. I _sort_ of get how it's working but as we add on to it 

The `*chars` side car on ObjString. As we dip down into this lower level, "primitives" like string (and dictionaries -- coming up in the queue) start to take a much, much more involved form. This makes sense, but it's interesting comign from my higher level mindset. It takes a lot of work to do seemingly simple things! I'm grateful for the language hackers that have gone before to pave this way for me. It's also an encouragement for myself that sometimes simple isn't easy but it can be worth it as a force multiplier.


Var args. Again `c` shows how seemingly simple things in other languages `(args: String...)` require _a library_ to accomplish in `c` 😄 

Overall: I'm starting to get why people enjoy writing in `c`. The amount of control is amazing. Do I want this much control? Not really 😅 but it helps me better see how `rust` and other newer systems languages have such a draw: you get more control with less risk. That's pretty compelling!

author: thosam1
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a comprehensive AI analytics backend for the PV monitoring platform, enabling natural language queries against solar data through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.

### Core Architecture

**Python MCP Server (`ai/`)**
- FastMCP server running on port 4000 with SSE transport
- Modular architecture with `tools/`, `models/`, `queries/` separation
- Structured logging with `structlog` for observability
- Retry logic with `tenacity` for database resilience
- Pydantic-based configuration with environment variable support

**NestJS AI Module (`backend/src/ai/`)**
- Multi-provider LLM support via Vercel AI SDK v5 (Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI)
- MCP client with SSE transport connecting to Python server
- Streaming chat endpoint (`POST /ai/chat`) with tool calling
- `render_ui_component` pass-through tool for frontend chart generation

### MCP Tools (10 total)

| Tool | Category | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `list_loggers` | Discovery | Find available inverters with data ranges |
| `analyze_inverter_health` | Diagnostics | Detect daytime outages (power=0 when irradiance>50) |
| `get_power_curve` | Analytics | Get timeseries data for charting |
| `compare_loggers` | Analytics | Multi-logger comparison on metrics |
| `calculate_financial_savings` | Financial | Money saved, CO2 offset, trees equivalent |
| `calculate_performance_ratio` | Performance | System efficiency vs theoretical output |
| `forecast_production` | Forecasting | Predict future energy from historical data |
| `diagnose_error_codes` | Diagnostics | Scan metadata for errors with fixes |
| `get_fleet_overview` | Aggregation | Site-wide status and production metrics |
| `health_check` | Monitoring | Service and database health verification |

### Frontend Components

**DynamicChart Component**
- AI-controlled chart generation (generative UI pattern)
- Supports 6 chart types: area, bar, line, scatter, pie, composed
- Solar-themed color palette with dual Y-axis support
- 44 comprehensive tests covering all scenarios

### Security & Quality

- SQL injection prevention via parameterized queries
- Proper TypeScript types (no `any` casts)
- 465 total tests passing (440 backend + 25 AI)
- Zero lint errors/warnings

### Infrastructure

- Docker Compose service for AI server with health checks
- Seed data script generating 10,080 records across 5 loggers
- Test data includes simulated anomalies and error codes

## Test plan

- [x] AI unit tests pass (`cd ai && pytest tests/ -v`) - 25 tests
- [x] Backend unit tests pass (`cd backend && npm test`) - 440 tests
- [x] Backend lint passes (`cd backend && npm run lint`) - 0 errors
- [x] MCP tools tested with real database data via Claude Code
- [x] Docker services start correctly (`docker-compose up -d`)

## Files Changed

- `ai/` - New Python MCP server (10 tools, models, queries, tests)
- `backend/src/ai/` - New NestJS AI module (controller, service, MCP client)
- `frontend/src/components/dashboard/dynamic-chart.tsx` - Generative UI component
- `docker-compose.yml` - AI service configuration
- `backend/src/database/seeds/seed-test-data.ts` - Test data generation

body:
Adds tab-completion functionality to the goodass CLI for improved user experience when selecting items from tables or selecting files.

## New Features

### Tab Autocomplete Support
- **Settings Menu**: Added tab completion for SSH private key path selection with full filesystem navigation
- **Host Management**: Added tab completion for removing hosts with `user@host` format support
- **User Management**: Added tab completion for user email selection in all user management operations
- **Key Access Management**: Added tab completion for removing access entries in the deepest layer of user key access management

## Code Refactoring

### New Modules Created
- **`autocomplete.py`**: Centralized tab-completion functionality with path completion, list-based completion, multi-word completion support, and Windows compatibility
- **`utils.py`**: Extracted utility functions (`signal_handler`, `exit_gracefully`, `generate_ssh_keypair`)
- **`settingsManager.py`**: Extracted settings management functions with tab completion support

### Code Improvements
- Added `non_interactive_fix_keys()` function to `keyManager.py`
- Reduced `cli.py` from ~470 lines to ~190 lines through modularization

## Usage Notes

- Press `Tab` to cycle through available completions when prompted
- Autocomplete for hosts and key access is only available for **removal** operations (not adding new entries)
- Path completion supports `~` expansion and directory navigation

## Compatibility

- Autocomplete requires the `readline` module (included by default on Linux/macOS)
- On Windows, the application gracefully falls back to standard input without completion

## Documentation

- Added `CHANGELOG.md` with release notes for version 0.0.6

- Fixes Nidhil-stack/GOODASS#25

body:
## Summary

Addresses multiple issues identified during comprehensive code review, including a bug fix, security improvements, performance optimizations, and code quality enhancements.

## Changes Made

**Bug Fixes:**
- Fix incorrect line number conversion in `deadcode.go:1245` - was using `string(rune(line))` which produces wrong output for line numbers > 127, now uses `strconv.FormatUint`
- Replace manual `itoa()` function with `strconv` stdlib functions

**Security:**
- Add path traversal protection in scanner to prevent symlink escapes outside root directory
- Change cache directory permissions from 0755 to 0700 (owner-only access)
- Add bounds checking to `GetNodeText` to prevent panic on invalid byte offsets

**Performance:**
- Fix BFS queue implementation in dead code analyzer to use index-based traversal instead of O(n) slice reslicing per dequeue

**Code Quality:**
- Add `Config.Validate()` method with comprehensive range validation for all numeric config values
- Extract shared `IsTestFile` and `IsVendorFile` functions to `testutil.go` to reduce duplication across analyzers

## Testing

- All existing tests pass
- Added 10 new test cases for config validation covering edge cases and error messages
- Pre-push hooks verified: fmt, tidy, lint, test all pass

body:
Admins need to create players without Clerk accounts to track historical game sessions for players who have left a group.

### Backend
- New `createFakePlayer` mutation on player router using `groupAdminProcedure`
- Creates player with `clerkId: null` and optional email
- Validates nickname uniqueness
- Auto-adds player to group with `ACCEPTED` status
- Added `getProfileImageUrl` helper function for consistent avatar handling

### Frontend
- New "Create Fake Player" form section in Admin view (name, nickname required; email optional)
- Purple "Fake Player" badge on user cards for players without `clerkId`
- Bot avatar (`/public/bot-avatar.svg`) displayed for fake players instead of "image not found"
- Replaced page reloads with tRPC cache invalidation for smoother UX when performing admin actions

```typescript
createFakePlayer: groupAdminProcedure
  .input(z.object({
    name: z.string().min(1),
    nickname: z.string().min(1),
    email: z.string().optional(),
    groupId: z.string()
  }))
  .mutation(async ({ ctx, input }) => {
    const player = await ctx.prisma.player.create({
      data: { name: input.name, nickname: input.nickname, email: input.email || null, clerkId: null }
    });
    // Adds to group with ACCEPTED status for immediate use in game sessions
  })
```

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
Patch L.DomEvent.off to swallow errors on canvas element cleanup

In JSDOM/Node environments with @napi-rs/canvas, Leaflet can fail to remove event listeners from canvas elements because they lack `removeEventListener`. Leaflet then falls back to `detachEvent` (IE legacy path), which also doesn't exist, causing a crash.

This patch wraps `L.DomEvent.off` to swallow "detachEvent is not a function" errors, preventing the crash while allowing normal event removal to proceed.

* Added `src/polyfills/dom-event.ts` with the patch logic.
* Updated `src/index.ts` to apply the patch during initialization.
* Verified with reproduction test case.

**Título del Pull Request:**
feat: Implementa el módulo de Gestión de Cambios (ITIL Change Management)

---

### 📝 Descripción General

Esta implementación introduce el nuevo módulo de **Gestión de Cambios (Change Management)**, siguiendo las **mejores prácticas de ITIL**.

El propósito estratégico es proporcionar un proceso formal y estructurado para manejar todos los cambios en el entorno de la aplicación, desde su **solicitud (CDC)** hasta su **aprobación** y **ejecución**. Esto asegura una **reducción de riesgos** e interrupciones, mejorando la estabilidad y la calidad de los servicios de TI.

---

### 📜 Resumen de Cambios

#### ✨ Funcionalidad Principal
- **Módulo de Gestión de Cambios (CDC):** Se introduce una nueva sección principal en la aplicación dedicada exclusivamente a la gestión de solicitudes de cambio.
- **Listado de Solicitudes:** Se crea un componente de tabla para mostrar un **listado de todos los Change Requests (CDC)**, permitiendo una visión general del estado y el ciclo de vida de cada cambio.
- **Detalle de Solicitud (CDC):** Un componente de detalle permite visualizar toda la información asociada a una solicitud específica (justificación, impacto, plan de rollback, etc.).

#### 🔧 Mejoras Técnicas y Arquitectura
- **Integración de Rutas:** Se ha actualizado el *router* principal para incluir las rutas necesarias (`/cambios`, `/cambios/:id`) y exponer la nueva funcionalidad.
- **Sistema de Tipos (TypeScript):** Se han definido **nuevos tipos de datos (`types/change-request.ts`)** para el objeto `ChangeRequest` (o CDC), garantizando la consistencia y la seguridad del tipado en toda la aplicación.
- **Navegación (UI):** Se integró el nuevo módulo en el componente de **navegación principal (`Sidebar`)**, bajo el título **"Gestión de Cambios"**.

---

### ✅ ¿Cómo se ha probado esto?
Para verificar el correcto funcionamiento del nuevo módulo:

1. Inicia sesión como un usuario con el rol de `administrador`.
2. Navega a la nueva sección **"Gestión de Cambios"** en el *sidebar* (o a la ruta `/cambios`).
3. **Verifica el Listado:** Confirma que se muestre correctamente la tabla con la lista de solicitudes de cambio.
4. **Verifica el Detalle:** Haz clic en una solicitud de la lista y verifica que se cargue la página de detalles, mostrando la información específica de la solicitud.

body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to the Klein–Gordon simulation toolkit, expands documentation, and adds new features for inhomogeneous PDEs and testing. The most important changes are grouped below by theme.

**Documentation and Project Scope**

* Major rewrite and expansion of `README.md`: now describes the research goals, project scope, development environment, simulation examples, troubleshooting, and contribution guidelines. It clarifies objectives and future aims for the codebase.

**Simulation Features and Examples**

* Added a new example script `examples/klein_gordon/1d_step_mass.py` that demonstrates a 1D Klein–Gordon simulation with a spatial mass step, including all setup, evolution, and plotting logic.
* Refactored `examples/klein_gordon/1d_gaussian_pulse.py` to modularize simulation setup, improve observer safety (checks for non-finite data), and enhance plotting (centered colormap, improved output naming). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ba008e1694a9622e7ff64482c9e2e1a7c2424275e42804c700bb53d56dcc448cR29-R67) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ba008e1694a9622e7ff64482c9e2e1a7c2424275e42804c700bb53d56dcc448cL54-R117) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ba008e1694a9622e7ff64482c9e2e1a7c2424275e42804c700bb53d56dcc448cL99-R157) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ba008e1694a9622e7ff64482c9e2e1a7c2424275e42804c700bb53d56dcc448cR7) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-ba008e1694a9622e7ff64482c9e2e1a7c2424275e42804c700bb53d56dcc448cL40-R80)

**Testing and Validation**

* Added a new test `tests/test_step_matches_homogeneous.py` which verifies that the inhomogeneous Klein–Gordon PDE with a constant mass profile matches the homogeneous case, ensuring correctness of the new PDE implementation and mass profile utilities.

**API and Package Structure**

* Updated `torsion_gertsenshtein/kgsim/__init__.py` to expose new PDEs (`InhomogeneousKGPDE`), mass profile utilities (`step_region_1d`, `constant_field`), and ensure they are available for import and use in examples/tests.

**Miscellaneous**

* Expanded the spell checker dictionary in `cspell.json` to cover new terminology and code identifiers relevant to the project (e.g., "hyperbolicity", "KGPDE", "llvmlite", "Mathematica", "rtol").

- This enables private security implementations to replace the reference plugin without modifying the main codebase
- The registry supports priority-based override where higher priority plugins win

## Changes

### Public Package (`pkg/`)
- `pkg/plugin/interfaces.go` - Core Plugin, Resettable, ShadowStateProvider interfaces
- `pkg/plugin/context.go` - Context struct for plugin initialization  
- `pkg/plugin/registry.go` - Global registry with priority-based override
- `pkg/plugin/registry_test.go` - Comprehensive tests (98.4% coverage)
- `pkg/ha/interfaces.go` - Public HA client interface
- `pkg/ha/adapter.go` - Adapter wrapping internal ha.Client
- `pkg/state/interfaces.go` - Public state manager interface

### Reference Security Plugin
- `internal/plugins/security/register.go` - Plugin registration with `init()` using PriorityDefault

### Documentation
- `docs/architecture/PLUGIN_SYSTEM.md` - Complete design and implementation guide

## How Override Works

1. Public plugin registers with `PriorityDefault` (0)
2. Private plugin (in separate repo) registers with `PriorityOverride` (100)
3. Higher priority plugin wins and is used

```
Plugin "security" registered (priority 0)
Plugin "security" being overridden (priority 0 -> 100)
Starting plugin: security (Private security plugin)
```

**Summary**

This PR adds comprehensive tests for the `AgendaFolder.creator` GraphQL field resolver to bring [src/graphql/types/AgendaFolder/creator.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/shreyas/Downloads/Talawa-API/talawa-api/src/graphql/types/AgendaFolder/creator.ts:0:0-0:0) to 100% code coverage as requested by the issue.

The new tests live in:

- [test/graphql/types/AgendaFolder/creator.test.ts](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/shreyas/Downloads/Talawa-API/talawa-api/test/graphql/types/AgendaFolder/creator.test.ts:0:0-0:0)

They invoke the actual resolver through the built GraphQL schema (`schemaManager.buildInitialSchema()` → [AgendaFolder](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/shreyas/Downloads/Talawa-API/talawa-api/test/graphql/types/AgendaFolder:0:0-0:0) → [creator.resolve](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/shreyas/Downloads/Talawa-API/talawa-api/src/graphql/types/AgendaFolder/creator.ts:9:3-116:4)) and cover the following branches:

- Unauthenticated client → `TalawaGraphQLError` with `extensions.code = "unauthenticated"`.
- Authenticated client but current user not found in DB → `unauthenticated`.
- Event not found for `parent.eventId` (data corruption scenario) → logs the expected error message and throws with `extensions.code = "unexpected"`.
- Authenticated user who is neither a global admin nor an org admin and has no membership → `extensions.code = "unauthorized_action"`.
- Authenticated user with a non-admin membership in the organization → `unauthorized_action`.
- Authorized administrator where `parent.creatorId` is `null` → resolver returns `null`.
- Authorized caller where `parent.creatorId === currentUserId` → resolver returns the current user object.
- Authorized organization administrator where `parent.creatorId` is a different user → resolver fetches and returns that creator user.
- Authorized caller where the creator record is missing (data corruption) → logs the expected error message and throws with `extensions.code = "unexpected"`.

No production resolver logic was modified; this PR only adds tests and includes the auto-updated schema/docs (`gql.tada.json`, docs under `docs/docs/auto-schema`, etc.) generated by the existing lefthook/pre-commit tooling.

## Rationale for this change

All `TableProvider` implementations must support the `projection` argument of the `scan` method. This was not the case in `CteWorkTable`.

## What changes are included in this PR?

Minimal implementation of the projection support. The projection applied before the plan node return results. It might be nice to push it further inside of the recursion implementation to reduce memory consumption but I preferred to keep the fix minimal.

I have not figured out yet a nice SQL query to trigger an error without this change. Some existing queries in `cte.slt` have set projection (i.e. not `None`) so the code is very likely working. There is also a test on the projection itself in `WorkTableExec`

author: copilot
body:
FUZZBUNCH was written for Python 2.6, which is no longer available in modern environments. This PR migrates the codebase to Python 3.12.

## Syntax Migration
- `print` statements → `print()` functions
- `raise Exception, "msg"` → `raise Exception("msg")`
- `except E, e:` → `except E as e:`
- `raw_input()` → `input()`
- `0666` → `0o666` (octal literals)
- `print >>file, msg` → `print(msg, file=file)`
- Fixed `sys.platform == 'linux2'` check (Python 3 uses `'linux'`)
- Regex patterns use raw strings (`r"..."`) to avoid escape warnings

## Platform-Specific Dependencies
Made Windows-specific binary imports (`pytrch`, `exma`) optional with graceful degradation:

```python
try:
    import pytrch as trch
    from pytrch import TrchError
except ImportError:
    print("Warning: pytrch module not available, some functionality will be limited")
    trch = None
    class TrchError(Exception):
        pass
```

Plugins requiring these binaries fail cleanly with warnings rather than crashing the framework.

## Error Handling
- Added directory existence checks before plugin enumeration
- Fixed exception string concatenation: `raise Exception("Invalid ") + prompt` → `raise Exception("Invalid " + prompt)`
- Corrected variable scoping issues in log.py and util.py

## Limitations
Windows-specific binaries (`.pyd`, `.dll`) are unavailable on Linux. Exploits depending on TRUANTCHILD/EXPLOITMANAGER will not load, but the framework remains functional for other operations.

Documentation in `PYTHON3_MIGRATION.md` details changes and known limitations.

This pull request introduces several enhancements and refactors across the backend API, focusing on authentication, alert management, audit log statistics, and firewall rule handling. The most significant changes include a migration to Supabase JWT-based authentication, improvements to the alert API for frontend compatibility, expanded audit log statistics, and schema updates for firewall rules. Additionally, a new IP management endpoint has been registered.

**Authentication overhaul:**

* Replaced hardcoded user authentication with Supabase JWT verification, including role determination based on email, secure token validation, and updated user info endpoints. Legacy login logic and password handling have been removed for security and maintainability. (`containers/backend/api/v1/endpoints/auth.py`)

**Alert API improvements:**

* Refactored alert response models for frontend flexibility, added new fields (`alert_id`, `destination_port`, `protocol`, `is_resolved`, `analyst_comments`), and switched to using dictionaries for alert serialization. Updated logic for status and resolution handling, including bulk status updates and the removal of obsolete fields. (`containers/backend/api/v1/endpoints/alerts.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL4-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfR21-R48) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfR105-R127) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL137-R168) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL155-R186) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL177-R200) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL191-R239) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL226-R259) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL252-R287) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-6ad38e6635e6ea9a4b5db43a65fba27df0287eaacf00a44721ed3693ed4cfecfL281-R313)

**Audit log statistics expansion:**

* Added `total_vnc_type_distribution` to audit log stats, providing all-time VNC type counts alongside time-filtered stats for more comprehensive monitoring. (`containers/backend/api/v1/endpoints/audit_logs.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6fcc9b5f5ee004e5ac2c74eaa96d6e307ceb84e147c4851ece429fb95f897080R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6fcc9b5f5ee004e5ac2c74eaa96d6e307ceb84e147c4851ece429fb95f897080R95-R102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6fcc9b5f5ee004e5ac2c74eaa96d6e307ceb84e147c4851ece429fb95f897080R139)

**Firewall rule schema update:**

* Standardized firewall rule output fields, including explicit `destination_ip`, `source_port`, `destination_port`, and `protocol`, and removed legacy meta field handling for clarity and frontend compatibility. (`containers/backend/api/v1/endpoints/firewall.py`)

**API endpoint registration:**

* Registered the new `ip_management` endpoint with the main API router for IP management functionality. (`containers/backend/api/v1/api.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9ee9891a034e5cc4a8a0fee09466097a65b8fd141108d157065af615bf0d3f40L2-R2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9ee9891a034e5cc4a8a0fee09466097a65b8fd141108d157065af615bf0d3f40R13)This pull request introduces a major refactor to the authentication and logging systems, transitioning backend and frontend authentication from hardcoded credentials to Supabase JWT-based authentication. It also standardizes backend logging timestamps to IST (Indian Standard Time) and updates frontend navigation and hooks to align with the new authentication flow and log naming conventions.

**Authentication Overhaul (Backend & Frontend):**

* Replaced hardcoded user authentication with Supabase JWT-based authentication in `auth.py`, including dynamic role assignment based on email and secure token verification using the Supabase JWT secret. The `/login` endpoint is removed, and `/me` now derives user info from the Supabase token.
* Updated the frontend authentication hook (`useAuth.js`) to use Supabase for login, logout, registration, and session management, removing reliance on local storage and Axios for auth state.
* Modified the API service (`api.js`) to automatically attach the Supabase access token to outgoing requests, ensuring secure backend communication.

**Log Download and Token Verification:**

* Added JWT token verification for log archive downloads, allowing secure browser downloads via token query parameters in `log_archives.py`.

**Timezone Standardization in Backend Logging:**

* Introduced utility functions in `settings.py` to get current time in IST and convert UTC to IST, and refactored all logging and archiving operations in `vnc_log_collector.py` to use IST timestamps instead of UTC. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-92e0eed50966fc9ec176d5a46bd7c5d3822e57e195538e06977e644f1232b716R3-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d0d0e24897d5499b3f3dd65b4684d1d4ea056861edf47a146f19b7902ae3dd93R26) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d0d0e24897d5499b3f3dd65b4684d1d4ea056861edf47a146f19b7902ae3dd93L55-R70) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d0d0e24897d5499b3f3dd65b4684d1d4ea056861edf47a146f19b7902ae3dd93L122-R123) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-d0d0e24897d5499b3f3dd65b4684d1d4ea056861edf47a146f19b7902ae3dd93L141-R142) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-d0d0e24897d5499b3f3dd65b4684d1d4ea056861edf47a146f19b7902ae3dd93L152-R160) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-d0d0e24897d5499b3f3dd65b4684d1d4ea056861edf47a146f19b7902ae3dd93L170-R172) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-d0d0e24897d5499b3f3dd65b4684d1d4ea056861edf47a146f19b7902ae3dd93L208-R209)

**Frontend Navigation and Log Naming:**

* Renamed "Audit Logs" to "VNC Logs" throughout the frontend (sidebar, routes, imports) to better reflect the content and align with backend changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a2215ed3db7b719b7be4477bfd91afa859cd72963348603093e70b0e82d1e719L12-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2215ed3db7b719b7be4477bfd91afa859cd72963348603093e70b0e82d1e719L275-R283) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c3848be484c5b6016a8d3059819c911187d57d984d2de0d824018530961e1bedL82-R82)

---

- Migrated backend authentication from hardcoded users to Supabase JWT verification, removed `/login`, and implemented role assignment based on email in `auth.py`.
- Refactored frontend authentication (`useAuth.js`) to use Supabase for all auth operations and session management.
- Updated API service to attach Supabase tokens to requests for secure backend access.

author: miguelarios
body:
## Problem When downloading new videos, we observed misleading warnings in the logs: ``` WARNING: Missing upload_date for video 5CNr36no5TI (Aprende Peque con Isa - Aprende los Colores...) ``` **Root Cause:** 1. Video discovery uses **flat extraction** for performance (fast, lightweight) 2. Flat extraction only provides basic metadata: `id`, `title`, `url` 3. **Does NOT include `upload_date`** - that requires full extraction 4. Warning was firing **before download** when upload_date is always missing 5. After yt-dlp downloads, it writes `.info.json` with full metadata 6. But we **never read it back** to populate the database **Impact:** - Database records had `NULL` or empty `upload_date` - Cleanup logic couldn't properly sort videos by age - False warnings appeared for every new download - Could delete wrong videos (newest instead of oldest) ## Solution ### 1. Added Helper Method ```python def _extract_upload_date_from_info_json(self, video_file_path: str) -> Optional[str]: """Extract upload_date from .info.json created by yt-dlp""" ``` ### 2. Backfill After Download After successful download and file verification: 1. Check if `upload_date` is missing 2. Read `.info.json` from disk 3. Extract `upload_date` field 4. Update database record 5. Commit with populated `upload_date` ### 3. Removed Premature Warning - Removed warning before download (always false positive) - Only warn if `.info.json` extraction actually fails (rare) ## Benefits ✅ **upload_date populated immediately** after each download ✅ **Cleanup can properly sort** videos by age ✅ **No more false warnings** in logs ✅ **Minimal overhead** - one disk read per download (~1-5ms vs minutes of video download) ## Testing Plan - [x] Code implemented and committed - [ ] Trigger manual download from web UI - [ ] Verify no warning appears during download - [ ] Verify upload_date is populated in database after download - [ ] Run cleanup and verify oldest videos are deleted (not newest) - [ ] Test in production environment ## Technical Details **Performance:** - One disk read per video (minimal overhead) - .info.json file is small (~10-50KB JSON) - Read only happens once per video - All future queries use database (fast) **Flow:** ```mermaid graph LR A[Discovery
flat extraction] --> B[Create Download
upload_date=''] B --> C[yt-dlp downloads
creates .info.json] C --> D[Read .info.json
extract upload_date] D --> E[Update DB
upload_date populated] E --> F[Cleanup can sort
by upload_date] ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

This pull request introduces a complete chat and messaging feature into the application, integrating Firebase for real-time communication and user management. It adds all necessary data models, UI components, navigation updates, and Gradle dependencies to support chat conversations, user lists, and typing indicators, as well as the underlying logic for sending and receiving messages.

**Firebase Integration and Gradle Updates**
* Added Firebase configuration via `google-services.json` and updated `app/build.gradle.kts` to include Firebase and Google Services plugins and dependencies, enabling Firestore and Auth for chat features. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e9afb781b1eb66802d1c01b2209209ac0e527cbaf766bb382528268a9e530140R1-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8cff73265af19c059547b76aca8882cbaa3209291406f52df1dafbbc78e80c46R6) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8cff73265af19c059547b76aca8882cbaa3209291406f52df1dafbbc78e80c46R93-R103)

**Data Models**
* Introduced `ChatMessage` and `MessageUser` data classes to represent chat messages and users in Firestore. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3cd83859b572bb25c618790ba1891905be888db504e1728d26f9c7f5dfca0f8bR1-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-df588aff3359d7a4152dcfab2382525a0a695fb929f85a5d6627df8db3b5b3ebR1-R6)

**Navigation and ViewModel Wiring**
* Refactored `MainActivity.kt` and `NavGraph.kt` to initialize and pass new `ChatViewModel` and `MessagesUserViewModel` instances, and updated navigation to support chat screens and conversation routes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e71b312148acf6e2431e661cd51ccc38af9053fc37a820742bd13b40ad41ff6dR4-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e71b312148acf6e2431e661cd51ccc38af9053fc37a820742bd13b40ad41ff6dR41-R57) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4194f1df1c6f522b025fac51635414dab7d3e39b723ae96dca8e0c3e724d34caR22-R41) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4194f1df1c6f522b025fac51635414dab7d3e39b723ae96dca8e0c3e724d34caL96-R117)

**UI Components for Chat**
* Added new composable components: `ChatBubble` for displaying messages, `TypingIndicator` for showing when a user is typing, and `UserRow` for the user list in the messaging UI. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-20a48d6c99bfb7d2be538978370aac260f41a138a5f76e8a124986b8c072e26cR1-R74) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d55861b872f672d240d0642bd98f588f329a19e8761ff5b856bb727c6f981066R1-R21) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8ab9a90f7c21a9b8dab6c0b4f280e7cdfb4f83f73078bfe25ea8496715d1725fR1-R27)

**Conversation Screen Implementation**
* Completely reworked `ConversationScreen.kt` to display chat messages in a scrollable list, handle sending messages and typing state, and integrate with Firebase for real-time updates. Also added a preview for UI development. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-72b1a9c7cbcd935ce10fa26aa60eae4bdff87019f2577f76b003975bc5603440L3-R113) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-72b1a9c7cbcd935ce10fa26aa60eae4bdff87019f2577f76b003975bc5603440R123-R236)

HelmRelease failing with `OCIRepository.source.toolkit.fluxcd.io "kubernetes-event-exporter" not found` due to missing namespace in `chartRef`.

## Changes

- **OCIRepository**: Added `ref.tag: "3.6.3"` to pin chart version
- **HelmRelease**: Added explicit `namespace: flux-system` to `chartRef`

```yaml
chartRef:
  kind: OCIRepository
  name: kubernetes-event-exporter
  namespace: flux-system  # Required - Flux defaults to flux-system lookup
```

Consistent with other HelmRelease patterns in this repo (e.g., `kured`).

> ```

> spec:
>   interval: 1h
>   layerSelector:
>     mediaType: "application/vnd.cncf.helm.chart.content.v1.tar+gzip"
>     operation: copy
>   url: oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/kubernetes-event-exporter
>   ref:

> ```

author: aryanranderiya
body:
This pull request refactors and streamlines the handling of todo and subtask creation and updates across the backend, focusing on improved model consistency, atomic database operations, and endpoint simplification. The changes replace older request models with unified ones, optimize subtask operations for atomicity and cache invalidation, and clean up endpoint routes for consistency.

**Todo and Subtask Model Refactoring:**

* Replaced usage of `TodoCreate` and `UpdateTodoRequest` models throughout the codebase with unified `TodoModel` and `TodoUpdateRequest` models for both creation and update operations. This affects agent tools, API endpoints, and service calls, ensuring consistent data handling and reducing redundancy. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8fa2b9bd57a6b1aa65acda50427e382ee1008af05d969fc0e0b7254832f6f467L11-L13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8fa2b9bd57a6b1aa65acda50427e382ee1008af05d969fc0e0b7254832f6f467L99-R99) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8fa2b9bd57a6b1aa65acda50427e382ee1008af05d969fc0e0b7254832f6f467L225-R225) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8fa2b9bd57a6b1aa65acda50427e382ee1008af05d969fc0e0b7254832f6f467L234-L235) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-3bdcb7a71f4cbe9f17fdbddbc6254128644bb659775a915b2411804cfabed34bL18-R41) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-3bdcb7a71f4cbe9f17fdbddbc6254128644bb659775a915b2411804cfabed34bL211-R218) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-3bdcb7a71f4cbe9f17fdbddbc6254128644bb659775a915b2411804cfabed34bL241-R248) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-3bdcb7a71f4cbe9f17fdbddbc6254128644bb659775a915b2411804cfabed34bL442-R435)

**Atomic Subtask Operations and Cache Invalidation:**

* Refactored subtask creation, update, and deletion endpoints (`create_subtask`, `update_subtask`) to use atomic MongoDB operations (`find_one_and_update` with array filters) instead of fetching and updating the entire todo object. This improves data integrity and performance, and includes cache invalidation and goal sync logic for completion status changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3bdcb7a71f4cbe9f17fdbddbc6254128644bb659775a915b2411804cfabed34bL554-R563) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3bdcb7a71f4cbe9f17fdbddbc6254128644bb659775a915b2411804cfabed34bL603-R627)

**API Endpoint Route Consistency:**

* Changed POST and GET routes for reminders and onboarding to use the root path (`""`) instead of `"/"`, aligning with FastAPI best practices for endpoint definition. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f399d9ca873d66af8266bbc9dae2f1d5d1ee82876549f96fbc0b444ac00be786L29-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f399d9ca873d66af8266bbc9dae2f1d5d1ee82876549f96fbc0b444ac00be786L223-R223) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-19bf0ad66024824c5a083ecbf09d705ef813dcea06faae1599bc6489eb9c3f8fR21-R31)

**Background Task and Service Handling:**

* Updated onboarding and OAuth endpoints to use new background task functions (`queue_personalization` instead of `_queue_personalization`, and removed `_queue_gmail_processing`), simplifying post-onboarding personalization and removing unused imports. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b3b36e96b245910db9a82d332423f94e6966bad5bd994b38a3b0fa5feb7fff53L23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b3b36e96b245910db9a82d332423f94e6966bad5bd994b38a3b0fa5feb7fff53L267-L268) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-19bf0ad66024824c5a083ecbf09d705ef813dcea06faae1599bc6489eb9c3f8fR21-R31) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-19bf0ad66024824c5a083ecbf09d705ef813dcea06faae1599bc6489eb9c3f8fL64-R50) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-19bf0ad66024824c5a083ecbf09d705ef813dcea06faae1599bc6489eb9c3f8fL82-R68)
